Okay, so this was requested of me so...here I go!

I'm using the black Pok3r with MX Clears. This is after about 30-45 minutes of use.

First things first: it feels very...solid. I don't know any other word to describe it. For such a small keyboard, it's actually quite hefty and will definitely not slide around on the table. Build quality is also top notch. The aluminum looks good, adds weight, and doesn't get in the way.

Key wobble could be worse, but it could certainly be a hell of a lot better. Mostly par for the course as far as that goes.

Customization is insaaaane. On the bottom, there's a switch to go from QWERTY, to Dvorack, to Wolmack. There is also a switch to set Caps Lock to Fn (though I won't be using that due to the fact that I'm one of those plebs that uses it instead of Shift). There's also buttons to change the polling rate of the keyboard. Fn+T sets it to 15 ms, Fn+G sets it to 10 ms, and Fn+B sets it to 5 ms. There's also ways to change the layers if you want different profiles.

Typing experience...feels like MX Clears. It's solid, nice, no frills. This is a no frills keyboard.

I have only two complaints:

(1) The backspace key makes a different, much more high pitched sound when pressed. Nothing too bad, just a bit annoying (I'm nitpicking here)

(2) The cable included in the packaging is a bit meh (short and rubberized, not braided.) That can be fixed quickly and easily. I did say I was nitpicking...

Seriously, from these veeeerrry limited first impressions, it's looking like this is my favorite small form factor board ever. If you have the money and are in the market for a new keyboard, go for this one.

I've spent some time looking over several videos and guides from Goulet and Jetpens. As a grad student my budget is limited with the quality of notebook/journal I can purchase. I'm looking for a fountain friendly paper and a durable cover. I tend to run around a lot and my notebooks tend to get beat up. Anyone have real world experience with them. Any recommendations? I haven't really tasted the world of notebooks that are out there, but my Moleskine classic is super durable (it still looks wonderful despite living in my enormous purse full of sharp and miscellaneous bric-a-brac) and works fine with my fountain pens. I get the ruled one. I don't know how cheap it is comparatively, or if I just write tiny and not often enough, but they certainly last long enough to warrant ~$15.

I have heard good things from my friends, but none of them have any experience with fountain pens. I do see them just about everywhere, so availablitiy won't be an issue. I'll definitely put them on my short list. Thanks for the feedback.

As far as an inexpensive hardbound journal goes, I've had great success with Black 'n Red notebooks. I use them for daily note taking, and the paper is generally FP ink-friendly, although the wetter inks might take a few more seconds to dry. Unlike my Moleskines, which seems to feather a good bit, the Black 'n Reds let you put down a crisp, clean line. The covers are durable as well - I have one that I've been using for a couple of years now, and it's still going strong.

Best of all, they're relatively cheap... around here (Colorado) you can get the 5x8 notebooks for about $10 at Staples or OfficeMax. They also have an 8x11 for a little more, but you may have to go online to find that one... around here they seem to be a little harder to find vs. the 5x8s.
